gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 13?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 13 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest DWD and ECMWF model runs converge on a Munich daytime maximum near 31°C today, driven by a stable high-pressure ridge and southwesterly warm advection under mostly clear skies and light winds. This setup produces strong surface heating that exceeds the city’s late-August climatological mean of 24–26°C, with ensemble guidance showing only modest spread around 30–32°C tied to minor boundary-layer moisture differences. Traders weight the narrow 30–31°C window most heavily given the model consensus and current observational trends. Resolution could shift only if an unforecasted increase in cloud cover or a sudden wind shift reduces peak insolation before official measurements finalize the daily high.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and AccuWeather point to a maximum temperature of 29–30°C in Tokyo on August 15, driven by the strengthening Pacific High that has produced above-normal summer temperatures across Honshu. This subtropical ridge promotes subsidence and clear to partly cloudy skies, yet scattered showers expected midday could limit peak heating by increasing cloud cover and evaporative cooling. Urban heat island effects from Tokyo's dense infrastructure add 1–2°C locally compared to rural baselines, while high humidity near 80% sustains warmth without altering the dry-bulb reading used for market resolution. Model consensus shows limited day-to-day variability at this lead time, with any shift in steering flow or precipitation timing the main variables that could favor 28°C or 31°C instead.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from the Met Office and ECMWF place London's August 15 maximum near 26–28°C under a mix of sunny intervals and scattered showers, with limited diurnal heating from modest Atlantic airflow and variable cloud. This tight clustering around 26–27°C reflects genuine uncertainty in afternoon convective development and exact frontal timing rather than strong divergence among models. After an intense early-August heatwave that pushed readings above 35°C, cooler maritime air has moderated conditions while still leaving the day slightly above the long-term August average. Traders weigh these factors against historical late-summer variability, where small shifts in boundary-layer moisture or insolation can swing the peak by 1–2°C. Official Met Office observations at 18:00 BST will resolve the market.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 15 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts project a Tokyo maximum of 29°C on August 15 under cloudy skies with scattered showers, aligning with the market's tight clustering around 29–30°C. Persistent cloud cover from a moderating Pacific high and possible precipitation timing limit daytime heating by reducing solar insolation, while urban heat island effects and humidity near 70–80% could add marginal warming. Minor shifts in forecast model runs—such as delayed showers or clearer intervals—differentiate outcomes between 28°C and 31°C, with historical mid-August normals near 31°C providing a baseline. Updated JMA guidance ahead of the date remains the key catalyst for trader adjustments.
